input: Research clinical trials for my chronic condition

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific condition determines which databases, disease communities, and trial registries to search — a rare disease vs. a common one requires very different search strategies.

Knowing whether the research is for the user themselves or for someone else (e.g., a child, parent, or partner) affects eligibility considerations, decision-making authority, and how personal the guidance should be.
Geographic location determines which trials the user can physically access and which national registries (ClinicalTrials.gov, EU Clinical Trials Register, etc.) are most relevant.
Current treatment status matters because many trials require participants to be treatment-naive, on specific medications, or at a particular disease stage — this filters eligibility dramatically.
The user's ability to travel or commit time to visits is a hard logistical constraint that immediately narrows the pool of viable trials.

Some users want any trial (expanded access, observational, interventional), while others have strong preferences about trial phase, experimental treatments, or placebo risk — this shapes which results to prioritize.
Understanding whether the goal is finding a potential treatment, contributing to science, accessing free care, or all three clarifies what 'a good result' looks like and how to evaluate options.

gold.taskTitle: Research clinical trials for chronic condition
gold.taskDescription: Find relevant, active clinical trials that match the user's specific chronic condition and personal circumstances.

questions.title: What specific condition are you researching trials for?
questions.description: Identify the exact diagnosis or condition name so research can be targeted to the right disease area, registries, and specialist communities.

questions.title: Is this research for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is the patient or acting as a caregiver/advocate, which affects eligibility framing and the tone of guidance.

questions.title: What country or region do you live in?
questions.description: Location determines which trial registries are most relevant and which studies the user can realistically participate in.

questions.title: What treatments are you currently on, if any?
questions.description: Current medications and treatment history are among the most common eligibility criteria that immediately include or exclude a patient from a trial.

questions.title: How much travel or time commitment can you manage?
questions.description: Trials vary from a single site visit to weekly appointments over years — knowing the user's capacity narrows the realistic options.

questions.title: Are you open to placebo-controlled or early-phase trials?
questions.description: Captures the user's risk tolerance and preferences around experimental interventions, placebo arms, and trial phase, which filters which studies to highlight.

questions.title: What is your main goal in joining a clinical trial?
questions.description: Understanding whether the priority is accessing a new treatment, contributing to research, receiving free care, or something else defines what a successful outcome looks like.
